summary: Summation No. 21 covers June 1947 in South Korea under USAMGIK. The dominant political story is the resumed U.S.-U.S.S.R. Joint Commission: Joint Communique No. 11 set out consultation procedure and questionnaires, 344 parties obtained copies by 19 June, a joint meeting was held in Seoul on 25 June and delegations moved to Pyongyang. The Interim Legislative Assembly finally passed the General Franchise Law on 27 June with a voting age of 23 after the Speaker's resignation crisis, while Rightists split over cooperation with the Commission. Economic sections report record April coal output, record May salt, rising Bank of Chosen note circulation (18.0 billion yen), the new Korean Foreign Exchange Bank, trade tables, railroads, power and prices. Social sections cover cholera immunization, 102,185 refugees from the north, textbooks, schools and press opinion. A historian gets full texts of Joint Commission documents and dense statistics.
highlights: The Joint Commission's Communique No. 11 of 12 June set out the method of consultation with Korean democratic parties, requiring a signed declaration upholding the Moscow Decision; 344 parties and organizations had obtained copies by 19 June.

On 27 June the Interim Legislative Assembly passed the General Franchise Law with a compromise minimum voting age of 23 (26 votes for 21, 40 for 23), after Speaker Kimm Kiu Sic and both Vice-speakers resigned on 3 June over a 25-year age requirement and withdrew resignations on 9 June.

The Hankuk Democratic Party decided to participate in Joint Commission consultation, splitting the Rightists who followed Syngman Rhee and Kim Koo; the South Korea Labor Party demanded their expulsion and chose Pak Hun Yung as its representative.
The Military Governor left for Washington on 21 June; Brigadier General C. G. Helmick acted in his place, and Korean became the official language of the Interim Government from 1 July.

Bank of Chosen notes in circulation rose 617,893,769 yen in June to 18,035,603,028 yen; the Korean Foreign Exchange Bank was created on 16 June with 500,000,000 yen capital; the revised Third Income Tax Law took effect.

April coal production of 31,318 metric tons was the highest since liberation, and May salt output of 32,207 metric tons a postwar high, while private-trade imports rose 521.8 percent in value with May imports about 600 million yen.
From 1 January to 28 June 102,185 refugees crossed south of the 38th parallel (24,501 in June); 74,637 were cared for in seven camps and 9,092 refugee housing units had been completed.
Criminal offenses in May rose to 10,226 from 8,540 in April, and 20,554 persons were held in prisons; more than 80 percent of police had no pre-liberation experience.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Google Books and library covers, title page of Summation No. 21 for June 1947, table of contents and list of 33 charts, maps and graphs.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of the month's political, economic and social developments, led by the Joint Commission consultations and the Franchise Law passed 27 June.

sections.title: Section 1. Political Activities
sections.summary: Speaker Kimm's resignation and the Franchise Law's 23-year voting age, the Rightist split over the Joint Commission, and the 25 June departure of delegations for Pyongyang.

sections.title: Section 2. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Rice transplanting of 2,824,466 acres, record coal and salt output, Pusan stevedore strike, 18.0 billion yen note circulation, and the Foreign Exchange Bank.

sections.title: Section 3. Social Activities
sections.summary: Cholera immunization, 102,185 northern refugees, 9,129,922 textbooks distributed, Joint Commission publicity and the new World News Report.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government, the Legislative Assembly, Joint Commission documents, foreign affairs, and law, police, prisons and fires for May and June 1947.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Acting Military Governor Helmick, Korean made official language, Assembly crisis over voting age, Rightist and Leftist maneuvers and full Joint Commission texts.

sections.title: Administration
sections.summary: Military Governor left for Washington 21 June; Helmick acted; Korean official language from 1 July; Ordinance Drafting Committee met 11 June.

sections.title: Korean Interim Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: Kimm and two Vice-speakers resigned 3 June, withdrew 9 June; the age vote (23 years favored by 40) led to final franchise law passage on 27 June.

sections.title: Political Developments
sections.summary: Hankuk Democratic Party joined consultation while Rhee's forces refused; the South Korea Labor Party demanded Rhee and Kim Koo be expelled and named Pak Hun Yung.

sections.title: U. S.-U. S. S. R. Joint Commission
sections.summary: Communique No. 11, method of consultation, Decisions 5 and 6 questionnaires, 344 applicants, 25 June meeting and departure for Pyongyang.

sections.title: Foreign Affairs
sections.summary: 121 travel permits issued in June to Chinese nationals being repatriated; 109 permanent-residence permits for Japanese wives, total 1,110.

sections.title: Section 2. Legal and Public Safety
sections.summary: Legislation, 23 June Rightist demonstrations, police experience, prison population of 20,554, 92 fires in May and Constabulary training.

sections.title: Legal
sections.summary: Ordinance No. 137 on inheritance tax and No. 140 limiting cattle slaughter, plus Public Act No. 2 on summer grain collection.

sections.title: Law and Order
sections.summary: Orderly Rightist demonstrations before Duk Soo Palace and the Soviet Consulate on 23 June demanded independence under Kim Koo.

sections.title: Police
sections.summary: Horses received from Japan; over 80 percent of police lack pre-liberation experience; policewomen assigned 1 June; most May offenses rose.

sections.title: Prisons
sections.summary: 669 prisoners released, total 1,056; 20,554 confined in May (17,669 sentenced); chart of criminal offenses since March 1946.

sections.title: Fires
sections.summary: 92 fires in May killed three, injured 49 and cost 116,404,472 yen; Kyonggi-do had the most fires.

sections.title: Internal Security
sections.summary: Fourth class of 102 opened at the Constabulary Officers' Training School 6 June; three-month refresher course began 16 June.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Natural resources, industry, commerce and rationing, with coal, salt, currency, trade, transport, utilities and price data.

sections.title: Section 1. Natural Resources
sections.summary: Rice transplanting from 16 June, New Korea Company operating 661,000 acres, fishing fleet census, April coal output of 31,318 tons.

sections.title: Agriculture
sections.summary: Fertilizer distribution of 57,953 tons, grain collection policy, New Korea Company income near 1 billion yen, Ordinance No. 140 protecting draft cattle.

sections.title: Fisheries
sections.summary: February fish landings of 25,027 metric tons; revised census counts 35,806 sailboats, 2,305 powered craft and 464,172 persons.

sections.title: Forestry
sections.summary: 38,323 chungbo of Kyonggi-do forest need erosion control; cutting rate is 2.7 times annual timber growth.

sections.title: Mining
sections.summary: Coal quota 35,500 tons versus 31,318 produced, stockpiles of 424,000 tons, 6,275 coal workers, and gold and silver output falling.

sections.title: Section 2. Industry
sections.summary: Salt at 32,207 tons, fertilizer production halted, paper, tobacco, leather and rubber output, silk and cotton figures, Pusan stevedore strike.

sections.title: Heavy Industries and Manufacturing
sections.summary: Noodle output of 512 tons, salt postwar high, 231 tons of paper, common brick at 6,000,000 pieces, adoption of metric measures.

sections.title: Textiles
sections.summary: Cocoon ceiling price set in May, raw silk production of 79,490 pounds in June, 47 mills producing 819,245 square yards of silk fabric.

sections.title: Labor
sections.summary: Pusan stevedore strike of 28 May settled by conciliation; Inchon labor school graduated 43; industrial immunization program progressed.

sections.title: Section 3. Commerce
sections.summary: Currency, bank deposits, revenues, Foreign Exchange Bank, vested property, trade tables, railroads, power, public works and communications.

sections.title: Finance
sections.summary: Notes reached 18,035,603,028 yen; deposits peaked at 23.0 billion yen; May revenue 1,022,599,160 yen versus expenditure 1,177,290,509; Foreign Exchange Bank created.

sections.title: Property Control
sections.summary: New Korea Company transferred all but one industrial property by 17 May; vested property sales reached 28,897,599 yen in May.

sections.title: Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Private-trade imports up 521.8 percent, lead and tungsten exports to the U.S., 30,880 tons of superphosphate from Japan, food imports and coal.

sections.title: Transportation
sections.summary: 6,452,743 rail passengers in May, 17,571 freight cars moved, 617 locomotives of which 271 operable; gasoline rose from 18 to 35 yen.

sections.title: Public Utilities
sections.summary: Power generated rose from 19 to 29 million kWh; plant capacity tables; permanent Public Utilities Committee appointed 3 June.

sections.title: Public Works
sections.summary: 362,831,452 yen spent in 1946-47 for 3,132,209 man-days; highway bridges completed; Seoul waterworks under 20 gallons per capita.

sections.title: Communications
sections.summary: Domestic mail and postal savings, 242 telegraph offices and 42,000 telephone subscribers, 12 radio stations, Civilian Supply Program I at 80 percent.

sections.title: Section 4. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Rice ration of .23 pound, summer-grain purchase prices, fertilizer allocations, petroleum distribution down 24 percent, falling Seoul retail and wholesale prices.

sections.title: Food
sections.summary: Summer grain prices set at 1,792 yen per suk of wheat and 2,064 for barley; 55,000 pounds of candy made into syrup for relief.

sections.title: Other Goods
sections.summary: 46 percent of fertilizer allocations sold, Korean coal prices up 30 to 50 percent, May allocations of matches, soap, shoes and cloth.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health, refugees and repatriation, education, culture and religion, and public information with press opinion.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Cholera immunization, 348 licensed veterinarians, 4,863 renewed doctors, flood relief, low-cost feeding, 102,185 refugees and 1,691 repatriated Koreans.

sections.title: Preventive Medicine
sections.summary: Cholera immunization of coastal areas and large inland cities completed; 1,011 typhoid cases in May.

sections.title: Veterinary Affairs
sections.summary: 348 veterinarians licensed, 49 of 50 Japanese horses passed quarantine, 37 milk plants and 715 slaughterhouses.

sections.title: Medical and Hospital Affairs
sections.summary: 4,863 doctors renewed licenses, 7,840 lepers in four institutions, 18 nursing teachers graduated 30 June.

sections.title: Supply
sections.summary: 25,288,900 cc of cholera vaccine produced since 1 March, 19,520,550 distributed; biologicals table.

sections.title: Narcotics
sections.summary: Taegu investigation arrested eight and seized 2.25 kilograms of opium.

sections.title: Public Assistance
sections.summary: Flood relief committees, low-cost feeding program, 24,501 refugees in June, seven camps with 74,637, housing for 9,092 completed.

sections.title: Repatriation
sections.summary: 1,691 Koreans repatriated 1-29 June, 1,546 from Japan; 199 Japanese repatriated from Korea.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Culture and Religion
sections.summary: Seoul National University morale, school finance survey, textbooks, adult education, libraries with 442,979 volumes, Youth Movement and Oslo delegates.

sections.title: Education
sections.summary: Survey of 73 elementary and 39 secondary schools, 9,129,922 textbooks, school statistics for 1 May, eight adult education conferences.

sections.title: Culture
sections.summary: Three Seoul libraries hold 442,979 volumes; Youth Movement about 150,000 members; Boy Scout handbook; support for Korean athletes at 1948 Olympics.

sections.title: Religion
sections.summary: Six delegates left 8 June for the World Conference of Christian Youth at Oslo; Americans gave $2,500 for a Seoul church organ.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Information
sections.summary: Leaflets on Joint Commission, 35 films reviewed, radio weather forecasts, franchise poll of 1,149 persons, World News Report and press comment.

sections.title: Information Programs
sections.summary: 600,000 leaflets airdropped and 400,000 more distributed; posters on food conservation and narcotics control.

sections.title: Motion Pictures
sections.summary: Newsreel on civil-service examinations released 9 June; 35 films reviewed for release.

sections.title: Radio
sections.summary: Joint Commission interviews broadcast 25 June; Korean Broadcasting System began daily weather forecasts.

sections.title: Press and Public Opinion
sections.summary: Poll: 55 percent of ages 20-39 favored a 20-year voting age; press split over Rhee, trusteeship and cooperation with the Commission.

sections.title: Map of Korea
sections.summary: Foldout map of Korea listed at the end of the report.

sections.summary: University of Virginia Alderman Library due-date slip, Google Books digitization pages and library barcode leaves.
